PO.4 Food Security & Dietary Diversity

Objective Definition : Vulnerable households have improved dietary diversity and nutritional status.

Household Dietary Diversity

Household dietary diversity is defined by asking the respondent which of the following 12 food groups did they consume within the last 24 hours including; grains, roots & tubers, pulses, vegetables, fruits, meat & poultry, eggs, fish & seafood, milk & dairy, oils & fats, packaged sweets or honey and miscellaneous others. Scores will range between 0 and 12. A score of 0 would reflect a household going a whole day without eating, a score of 12 suggests every listed food group was consumed within the household.

Note: During the pilot phase of groundswell, these questions only included the responding woman of the household in the wording. Future implementations will reflect the whole household.

% Households Reached minimum level of diversity (at least 5 food groups): 85.4%

FIES (Food Insecurity)

The Food Insecurity Experience Scale (FIES) assesses a households recent history of food security through 8 questions. For each question, the responding woman will answer whether or not the household exhibited certain events due to a lack of money or resources over the last 12 months. These include being unable to east healthy foods, skipping meals, and going a whole day without eating.

Each behaviour experienced increases the FIES score by 1, therefore lower scores represent greater food security while high scores reflect high insecurity. Households may additional be categorised based on which specific events they experienced.

  • Food Secure = No food insecure events experienced
  • Mildly Insecure = Experienced worrying about not having enough to eat, being unable to eat healthy food, eating only a few kinds of foods or skipping a meal
  • Moderately Insecure = Experienced eating less than they thought they should, running out of food or were hungry but not eat.
  • Severely Insecure = Experienced going a whole day without eating
